name: Hindustan Aeronautics Ltd
about: Hindustan Aeronautics Ltd (HAL), a 71.64% Government-owned Maha-Ratna CPSE, designs, manufactures, upgrades and provides lifecycle MRO for aircraft, helicopters, aero -engines, avionics /accessories and aerostructures, principally for India’s armed forces. [1]

statements.text: Revenue compounded 7.8% a year over 5 years (FY21→FY26); profit after tax 23.0%.
EBITDA margin expanded 610 bps over 5 years (23.5% → 29.6%).
Revenue growth accelerated from 11% to 15% YoY over the last 4 quarters.
Over 5 years: ₹36,009 cr of profit, ₹51,775 cr of operating cash — conversion 1.44x.

ledger.quote: Yes, it will be in the range of 10% to 12% minimum.
ledger.statement: FY27 revenue growth of 10-12% at minimum
ledger.speaker: Barenya Senapati

check.basis: FY27 to date (2 of 4 quarters) YoY

ledger.evidence: Check: FY27 revenue growth to date (2 of 4 quarters) is 14.7% YoY against a 10-12% minimum, with Q1 at +14.4% and Q2 at +14.8%. H2 can grow as little as about 6-9% and still meet the guide.

ledger.quote: the EBITDA margin, we have always maintained around 30%, 31%, and it will be maintained
ledger.statement: EBITDA margin of around 30-31% maintained in FY27
ledger.speaker: Barenya Senapati

check.basis: FY27 EBITDA margin to date (2 of 4 quarters)

ledger.evidence: Check: FY27 EBITDA margin to date is 24.9% against a 30-31% guide, and Q2 FY27 was 22.8% (23.5% a year ago). Q4 is seasonally high (36.3% in Q4 FY26), but H2 would need roughly 35-37% to average 30%. The 'always maintained 30-31%' claim also contradicts the earlier 27% (G9) and 26-27% (G36) guides.

ledger.quote: That's 20, this year, we are planning to deliver
ledger.statement: Deliver about 20 LCA aircraft in FY27
ledger.speaker: Ravi Kota
ledger.evidence: Target of 20 LCAs in FY27. In the same call, management expected 'some delay... from a few places' because of supply-chain slowness (C5). An analyst noted the H2 revenue guide implies a single-digit LCA dispatch (C2). FY26 LCA deliveries were already delayed (C4), with about INR8,100 crore of inventory against LCAs not yet delivered (C3). No delivery count for H1 FY27 is in the inputs.

ledger.quote: we should be able to roll out Mark II
ledger.statement: Tejas Mk II rollout by March 2027
ledger.speaker: Ravi Kota
ledger.evidence: Tejas Mk II rollout by March 2027. The deadline has not arrived and there is no later call. This milestone replaced the earlier first-flight target of early CY2026 (G10).

ledger.statement: Invest about INR 12,000 crore in new manufacturing capacity by 2030
ledger.speaker: Ravi Kota
ledger.evidence: About INR12,000 crore of new-capacity capex by 2030. The facts have no capex figure and the horizon is about 3 years out.

ledger.speaker: Ravi Kota
ledger.evidence: Orders of about INR90,000 crore expected over 2 years from May 2026. The inputs contain no order-inflow data.

ledger.speaker: D.K. Sunil
ledger.evidence: Five-year capex of INR14,000-15,000 crore, repeated from Q4 FY24 (G13). Q4 FY26 instead cites INR12,000 crore by 2030 for new manufacturing projects (G5), possibly a narrower scope. Capex is not in the facts.

ledger.quote: we will be maintaining the operating profit to revenue at 27%

ledger.quote: the first flight of the prototype is expected next year, early next year, '26. And certification is typically three years, so '29.

context.speaker: Barenya Senapati
context.text: No. If you see, spares sales have actually come down by around INR500 crores to INR600 crores in the current financial year compared to the last financial year. But the repair and overhaul are almost at the same level because we have not added any new platform to our repair and overhaul activities. It's all the same platforms like ALH and -- maybe when the LCA will come up for repair and overhaul, maybe next year, and more of LCH, if it comes, then only it will be a significant increase in repair and overhaul we may have in the next financial year. Otherwise, if you see platforms are the same and then at the same level only, except for the escalation part, and other things which might be there.

context.speaker: Sumit Kishore
context.text: Good afternoon. My sincere regards and congratulations to Mr. Ravi for shouldering this huge responsibility for the nation in heading HAL. My first question is, the 10% to 12% revenue growth numerically in the second half of the year, how many LCAs are you sort of factoring in terms of dispatch? Because it appears to be a single-digit number, given the value per LCA. So -- and when I look at the inventory plus contract assets, that's almost INR490 billion. So what percentage of your inventory unbilled revenue is for the LCA program now? So maybe if you could address these 2 points as the first question.

context.speaker: Management
context.text: So, inventory for LCA is around INR7,500 crores. And if you look at the unbilled revenue, unbilled revenue is against the delivery that has already happened. It's not against the inventory. Whatever we have delivered because of the documentation and all those things, the non-receipt of documentation we could not bill it. So that has nothing to do with non-delivery of LCA. For Page 10 of 18 Hindustan Aeronautics Limited May 15, 2026 non-delivery of LCA, our inventory is around INR8,100 crores, if you include raw material and WIP.

We have achieved revenue from operations of INR33,050 crores for financial year 2025-'26 in comparison to INR30,981 crores in financial year 2024-'25. This is an increase of 7%, despite global aerospace supply chain disruptions. Deliveries of ALH helicopters, AL-35FP engines, RD-33 engines and ROH revenues helped offset delays in Tejas Mark-1A and HTT-40 programs. Our diversified portfolio has enabled balanced growth across segments. Our manufacturing revenue was INR9,227 crores, and ROH revenue was at INR20,524 crores.

Yes. See, if you see now the current global situation, whatever is there, I will not say disruption, but slowness is there. There is a slowness. But when we have discussions with them, and now we have started discussing with their Tier 1, Tier 2 vendors also, we are getting confident that we should be able to get the items. There may be minor delays, but we are confident that we will be getting within the time required for me to complete the platform and delivery. Because the current situation is like that, some delay is expected from a few places. Page 6 of 18 Hindustan Aeronautics Limited May 15, 2026

So, for example, the wings will come from L&T, the center fuselage will come from VEM, the rear fuselage will come from Alpha Tocol, the vertical fin and air intake, and the rudder will come from Tata TASL. So, that will add to this quantity. So, last year, we were able to get the first rare fuselage from Alpha Tocol. So, we expect that as these private sector players with our support ramp up and they start producing, we will be able to get further aircraft sets from the private sector. So, the expectation is that if we add about six from the private sector, we will have a capacity of almost 30 aircraft per annum.

As of now, we are working on a very tight schedule with all this. Many of these systems to get certified. We have already started build of the aircraft and the aircraft structure should be available, by June or in the next 3 to 4 months. And after that, the systems also, as and when it gets certified, it will get fitted into that, and we will be in a position to have the ground test and things like that happening in the next 8 to 10 months' time frame. So we are working towards meeting the delivery time lines. Probably even if there are going to be some sort of delays, it may not be very significant.
We are confident that we should be able to work on those delays and see that these aircraft are delivered as per the contracted delivery schedule.

And the current financial year also, we have been maintaining that it will be a single-digit growth only, and it will be at around the 9% is what we have achieved, but we are inching towards the double-digit growth, which we have promised to be there from FY '25 onwards. And we expect the -- from FY '25, it will be a double-digit growth. And after that, we expect the growth at around 12% to 13% and then stabilize at around 14% to 15%.

business.what_it_does: Aerospace and defence manufacturer. It builds aircraft and helicopters (Tejas LCA Mk-1A, HTT-40 trainer, ALH, LCH) and engines (AL-35FP, RD-33), and runs a large repair-and-overhaul (ROH) and spares business. It is developing Tejas Mk II and plans INR12,000 crore of new capacity by 2030. FY26 revenue from operations was INR33,050 crore, up 7% from INR30,981 crore. Manufacturing plus ROH account for about 90% of revenue; the inputs do not describe the remaining INR3,299 crore.

segments.name: Repair and overhaul (ROH), incl. spares
segments.comment: INR20,524 crore in FY26. Management says R&O was 'almost at the same level' as the prior year and spares fell INR500-600 crore. Growth depends on new platforms such as LCA and LCH entering overhaul.

segments.name: Manufacturing
segments.comment: INR9,227 crore in FY26. Tejas Mk-1A and HTT-40 delays were offset by ALH, AL-35FP and RD-33 deliveries. 20 LCAs are planned for FY27, and private-sector structures could take LCA capacity to about 30 a year.

narrative_vs_numbers.claim: In FY23, management promised double-digit growth from FY25, then 12-13%, stabilising at 14-15%.
narrative_vs_numbers.reality: The 3y revenue CAGR is 7.1% (5y 7.8%), and FY26 grew 6.8% against an 8-10% guide. Quarterly growth recovered to 14.4% and 14.8% in H1 FY27, the first quarters in the promised band.

narrative_vs_numbers.claim: 'The EBITDA margin, we have always maintained around 30%, 31%, and it will be maintained.'
narrative_vs_numbers.reality: Earlier guides were 27% (Q4 FY25) and 26-27% (Q4 FY23). H1 FY27 margin is 24.9%, Q2 was 22.8%, and the last four quarters range from 22.8% to 36.3%. TTM is 29.3%.

narrative_vs_numbers.claim: Unbilled revenue relates to deliveries already made and is held up by documentation, not by LCA non-delivery. LCA inventory is about INR8,100 crore.
narrative_vs_numbers.reality: The cash conversion cycle has stretched from 475 to 788 days in 3 years, which is consistent with deliveries not converting to billing. Historical cash generation is still strong: 5y FCF of INR42,432 crore and CFO/PAT of 1.44x.

narrative_vs_numbers.claim: Supply chain shows 'slowness' with only 'minor delays', and 20 LCAs will be delivered in FY27.
narrative_vs_numbers.reality: FY26 already absorbed Tejas Mk-1A and HTT-40 delays, and the Mk-2 first flight slipped from early CY2026 to a rollout target of March 2027. H1 FY27 revenue rose 14.7%, but the inputs give no LCA delivery count.

bull.point: H1 FY27 revenue rose 14.7% YoY against a 10-12% minimum guide, with Q1 at +14.4% and Q2 at +14.8%. Q2 PAT rose 16.0%, and TTM revenue is INR34,769 crore.

The balance sheet is effectively debt-free: borrowings are INR10 crore and D/E is 0.0. 5y FCF was INR42,432 crore, CFO/PAT 1.44x and ROCE 32%. The INR12,000 crore capex plan to 2030 is fundable from internal cash.

Management expects INR90,000 crore of orders over 2 years. About INR8,100 crore of LCA inventory is built and waiting to deliver, and four private suppliers (wings, centre fuselage, rear fuselage, fin) could lift LCA capacity to about 30 a year.

bear.point: Growth guidance keeps missing: FY26 grew 6.8% against 8-10%, the double-digit promise from FY25 was missed, and the 3y CAGR is 7.1% against a promised 12-13%. ROH, at 62% of revenue, was roughly flat in FY26 against an 8-9% target.

Margin is running well below the new guide: H1 FY27 was 24.9% against 30-31%, and Q2 was 22.8% against 23.5% a year earlier. The 30-31% anchor is itself higher than the 26-27% guided in earlier years.

Cash is getting stuck: the cash conversion cycle rose from 475 to 788 days in 3 years, with INR8,100 crore of inventory against undelivered LCAs. Programme dates have slipped (Tejas Mk-1A, HTT-40, Mk-2 first flight), and management flags further supplier delays.

questions: How many Tejas Mk-1A aircraft were delivered and billed in H1 FY27 against the 20 guided for FY27, and how much of the INR8,100 crore of non-delivery inventory has turned into revenue?
You said EBITDA margin has 'always' been guided at 30-31%, but Q4 FY25 guided 27% and Q4 FY23 guided 26-27%. Which is the real anchor, and what lifts H2 FY27 from the 24.9% run in H1?
The cash conversion cycle rose from 475 to 788 days in 3 years. How much of that is unbilled revenue waiting on documentation, what is the oldest item, and when does it convert to cash?
